s: A global ecommerce company has many data centers around the world. With the growth of its stored data, the company needs to set up a solution to provide scalable storage for legacy on-premises file applications. The company must be able to take point-in-time copies of volumes by using AWS Backup and must retain low-latency access to frequently accessed data. The company also needs to have storage volumes that can be mounted as Internet Small Computer System Interface (iSCSI) devices from the company's on-premises application servers. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Configure the tape gateway to store data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy AWS Backup to take point-in-time copies of the volumes.
Provision an Amazon FSx File Gateway and an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Deploy AWS Backup to take point-in-time copies of the data.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway in cache mode. Back up the on-premises Storage Gateway volumes with AWS Backup.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in cache mode. Deploy AWS Backup to take pointin-time copies of the volumes.

w.y: The requirements are iSCSI block volumes, low-latency access to frequently used data and point-in-time backups with AWS Backup. A Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode keeps the primary data in S3, caches hot data locally and presents iSCSI volumes. AWS Backup can back up those volumes directly as EBS snapshots.

o.A: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library for backup software, not mountable iSCSI volumes.
o.B: FSx File Gateway and S3 File Gateway present SMB or NFS file shares, not iSCSI block devices.
o.C: Correct: cached Volume Gateway provides iSCSI volumes with a local cache and is supported by AWS Backup.
o.D: File Gateway exposes NFS or SMB shares, not iSCSI volumes, and has no 'cache mode' volumes to snapshot.
